title.en: Days of mourning that will turn to yom tov

summary.en: After Shavuos the Mashgiach looks ahead to the fast for the massacres of Tach v'Tat in Sivan and to the Three Weeks. He says that when Moshiach comes these will be the happiest weeks of the year, describes a tzaddik who held a cup on Tisha B'Av to show how kiddush will be made then, and brings Zechariah's prophecy that the fasts will become days of joy.

title.en: Preparing for the low days amid great trials

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the week after Shavuos still belongs to the yom tov, then turns to the preparation for the coming low days: learning, davening, good middos and above all guarding the eyes and thoughts. The world's impurity is unprecedented, and it leads to doubts in emunah.

title.en: Doubts in emunah: ignore, don't answer

summary.en: Bringing the Or HaChaim that before Moshiach Jews will fall into the fiftieth gate of impurity, the Mashgiach explains why doubts are so common today. He calls them a 'bug' in the head, compares them to OCD, tells the story of the Vilna Gaon's advice to a man who saw a cross while davening, and concludes that one must ignore such thoughts and never debate them.

title.en: Emunah before Moshiach: climbing a smooth wall

summary.en: The Mashgiach cites tzaddikim that before Moshiach emunah will be as hard as climbing a smooth wall, and Rebbe Nachman of Breslov that a Jew with simple faith then will be as great a wonder as the Ba'al Shem Tov. The Satan fights with his last strength because he knows his end is near; one must pray for clear emunah and say the Ani Maamins.

title.en: Chevlei Moshiach and the Midrash about Paras

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the wars and troubles before Moshiach, the danger to Jews in Eretz Yisroel and everywhere, and Iran's wish for a bomb. He brings the Midrash that Paras will threaten to destroy the world and Hashem will tell the Jews not to fear, for the time of their redemption has come, and identifies Paras with Iran; one must prepare with Torah and mitzvos to greet Moshiach without shame.

title.en: The mitzvah to wait for Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that a person is asked whether he hoped for the salvation, and argues that saying 'ki lishuascha kivinu kol hayom' in davening or 'ki mechakim anachnu lach' in the Shabbos kedushah without truly waiting would be a lie before Hashem. The Chachamim instituted these words for ehrliche Yidden who really wait.

title.en: Moshiach hidden in Tamuz and Av; 'hinei Elokeinu zeh'

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Moshiach lies hidden in the months of Tamuz and Av, citing the Midrash that he is born on Tisha B'Av. Hashem asks through Tzefaniah that Jews wait for Him, and Yeshayahu's words 'hinei Elokeinu zeh kivinu lo' can be said only by one who truly hoped.

title.en: Remembering Yerushalayim; Moshiach can come any day

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Dovid HaMelech's oath 'im eshkacheich Yerushalayim', from which comes the custom of breaking a glass at the chuppah, and says one must constantly remember and pray for Yerushalayim. Moshiach is not tied to any time and can come any moment, even before the next Maariv.

title.en: Before its time; the spark of Moshiach in every Jew

summary.en: From the exile in Mitzrayim, foretold as four hundred years but ended after two hundred and ten, the Mashgiach shows that redemption can come early. He points to the wars of the time and the Gemara that Moshiach comes in the year after shemittah, says every Jew has a spark of Moshiach's soul to rectify, and closes that sad days can be turned into days of joy.

oneLiner.en: Speaking to bachurim before the summer, the Mashgiach explains how camp can be a place of kiddush Hashem: breaking one's will for Hashem, keeping away from politics and machlokes, tznius, helping friends, and coming to love Hashem by looking at the beauty of His creation.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by praising the bachurim for the kiddush Hashem they made on a recent Shabbos in Monsey, and tells them that camp too can bring either kiddush Hashem or, chas veshalom, the opposite. True mesiras nefesh, he explains, is giving up one's own will for Hashem's will, again and again. He warns against disobeying the camp staff, against arguing about rebbes and chassidus, and against politics, bringing a Rav who said that bachurim's involvement in politics is why gedolim no longer grow. From Dovid Hamelech's words in Tehillim 34 he shows that yiras Hashem means guarding one's tongue and seeking peace, not outward dress. He asks for tznius and for helping weaker friends with one's time. Then, using the Rambam, he describes coming to love Hashem by seeing creation in the country: sunsets, Barchi Nafshi, birds and animals, the story of Reb Shraga Feivel at the window, and Perek Shirah. He closes with being Hashem's shaliach and making berachos with kavanah.

en: Camp is a place where a bachur can make a great kiddush Hashem through hasmadah, davening with kavanah and guarding himself from aveiros, or, chas veshalom, the opposite.
Mesiras nefesh is not only giving up one's life; every time a Jew acts against his own will to do Hashem's will, that is mesiras nefesh and kiddush Hashem.
Bachurim should stay out of politics and arguments between chassidus'n and rebbes, and walk away when such talk begins.
Yiras Hashem, as Dovid Hamelech teaches it, is guarding one's tongue and seeking peace, not long peyos or a fine hat.
Following the Rambam, a person comes to love Hashem by contemplating His creation, which in the country is open to see while in the city it is hidden by buildings.
Hashem made the world not only practical but beautiful, so that people should enjoy it, and one must thank Him for that enjoyment.
Every food Hashem gave is both good and beautiful, so one should make berachos with kavanah and thank Him.

title.en: The Shabbos in Monsey and the camps ahead

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells the bachurim of the kiddush Hashem they made on a Shabbos in Monsey, as a rosh yeshiva reported that they brought a new spirit, rising early to learn and davening well. He tells them that in camp too one can make a kiddush Hashem or, chas veshalom, a chillul Hashem, and that kiddush Hashem is the greatest thing.

title.en: Mesiras nefesh: giving up one's own will

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that mesiras nefesh means overcoming one's own will for Hashem's will, something a person can do fifty or sixty times a year, asking Hashem for the strength. A bachur who conducts himself well and is an example to others makes a great kiddush Hashem; the opposite is losing patience and treating defiance of the camp staff as heroism.

title.en: Keeping away from machlokes and politics

summary.en: The Mashgiach warns bachurim meeting others from different chassidus'n not to argue over whose rebbe is greater, and not to get involved in the politics of Eretz Yisroel. He tells of bachurim who came to a Rav complaining about another party, and the Mashgiach answered that in his youth bachurim stayed out of politics, and that today's involvement is why gedolei Yisroel do not grow.

title.en: Dovid Hamelech teaches what yiras Hashem is

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that speaking against a whole community is far worse lashon hara than speaking against one Jew. He then brings Dovid Hamelech's call in Tehillim 34, 'Come, children, listen to me, I will teach you yiras Hashem', and shows from the next pesukim that yiras Hashem means guarding one's tongue and pursuing peace, not long peyos or fine clothes.

title.en: Tznius in camp and helping friends

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of tznius in camp, at the swimming pool and the showers, asks for takanos there, and tells bachurim to keep away from those who do not conduct themselves with tznius because it is contagious. He then asks them to help a weaker friend, bringing the Steipler that giving away part of one's learning time to help another is tzedakah.

title.en: Coming to love Hashem through His creation

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Rambam that the way to love Hashem is to contemplate His creation, and contrasts the city, where buildings hide it, with camp's fields, trees and flowers. He brings the berachah on blossoming trees, made so that people should enjoy them, and tells how he used to take his family up a hill to watch the sunset and say Barchi Nafshi, urging the bachurim to do the same after Minchah.

title.en: Why Dovid breaks out with 'Mah rabu'

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the tzaddikim's question why, in the middle of Barchi Nafshi, Dovid Hamelech interrupts with 'Mah rabu ma'asecha Hashem', and their answer that he was so overwhelmed by the beauty of creation that he could not hold back. He stresses that Hashem could have made the world merely practical but made it beautiful, and explains the zemer's words 'tzafra ve-ramsha' as the birds singing in the morning and the insects at night.

title.en: Reb Shraga Feivel at the window; the wisdom in creatures

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how his rebbe, Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz, davened looking out of a window in the country, and when someone pushed him to look into the siddur he answered that he was looking in, to what the siddur's pesukim describe. He then describes the wisdom Hashem put into birds, butterflies and squirrels, and brings Perek Shirah, where a frog told Dovid Hamelech that its song is greater.

title.en: A shaliach of Hashem; berachos with kavanah

summary.en: Connecting to Parshas Shelach, the Mashgiach says one must know he is a shaliach of Hashem sent to accomplish things. He then asks the bachurim to make berachos with kavanah, since Hashem could have fed people like a car with gasoline but gave food that is tasty and beautiful, and closes with blessings for a successful summer in learning, davening and health.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach explains that Moshe Rabbeinu fasted against Amalek for 'tomorrow', the last generations before Moshiach, and that Jews who keep their small flame burning in the storm winds of 1979 are themselves a miracle.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with a Midrash that Moshe Rabbeinu saw a great treasure in heaven and asked whom it was for, calls Purim the greatest Yom Tov, and speaks of Eliyahu HaNavi and Moshiach coming on Purim. He then turns to that day's reading of the war with Amalek: the Gemara says the word 'tomorrow' in Moshe's words to Yehoshua has no decision. The Mashgiach explains that Moshe fasted not only for that battle but for the decrees of our time, the great war with Amalek before Moshiach, since Hashem's war with Amalek runs from generation to generation. Moshe saw the Jews of later generations, and today every Jew who says Shema, learns a blatt Gemara or counts sefirah is a banner, 'Hashem nisi'. He ends with the Mishnah's miracles of the Beis HaMikdash: in 1979, with winds of pritzus and heresy, the small fire of Jewish service is not extinguished and its smoke rises straight to heaven.

en: The Mashgiach calls Purim the greatest Yom Tov.
Moshe Rabbeinu fasted not only for the battle with Amalek of his day but for the decrees of today, the great war with Amalek before Moshiach.
Hashem's war with Amalek continues from generation to generation.
Today every simple act of a Jew, saying Shema, learning a blatt Gemara, counting sefirah, is a banner of 'Hashem nisi', and Moshe fasted for these Jews.
Jews who come together in a world of heresy and pritzus are like the miracle of the Beis HaMikdash, where the fire was not extinguished and the wind did not scatter the smoke.

title.en: Opening: Purim and the coming of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens with a Midrash that Moshe Rabbeinu saw a great treasure in heaven and asked whom it was for. He calls Purim the greatest Yom Tov and speaks about Eliyahu HaNavi and Moshiach coming on Purim.

title.en: 'Tomorrow': Moshe's fast for our generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that 'tomorrow' in Moshe's words to Yehoshua has no decision, and explains that Moshe fasted for the decrees of our time, the great war with Amalek before Moshiach. Hashem's war with Amalek runs from generation to generation.

title.en: 'Hashem nisi': every Jew today is a banner

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that when Moshe raised his hands Yisrael prevailed, and that Moshe fasted for us in 1979. Moshe saw the Jews of later generations, and every Jew today who says Shema, learns a blatt Gemara or counts sefirah is a banner, 'Hashem nisi'.

title.en: The fire that was not extinguished

summary.en: The Mashgiach turns to the miracles of the Beis HaMikdash in the Mishnah: the fire on the altar was not put out and the wind did not scatter the smoke. In 1979, with storm winds of pritzus and heresy, Jews still come together, and their small fire and thin smoke rise straight to heaven.

catalogTitle: Thanking Hashem - An Endless Endeavor (מזמור לתודה)

oneLiner.en: Starting from Mizmor l'Sodah, the Mashgiach shows that thanking Hashem is an endless task: every breath, every hidden miracle and every rescue calls for thanks, and Hashem even arranged the miracle at the Yam Suf so that Jews could come back and thank Him there.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Mizmor l'Sodah and calls the chance to thank Hashem one of His greatest gifts. That is why each person says Modim d'Rabbanan himself, and why it ends with thanks for being able to thank. David HaMelech closes Tehillim with praise for every breath, and Nishmas admits that we could not thank even for one of His countless favors; the body alone is a daily miracle. The four who must thank in Tehillim 107 are only samples, and the Gemara requires ten people, two of them Rabbanan, for Birkas HaGomel: a wise man is needed to explain the kindness, and a second one shows there is always more to say. The short eating time of the korban todah increases pirsumei nisa, which leads to Chanukah, women's obligation in it, and gratitude as the root of avodas Hashem. He ends with the Chasam Sofer on why the Egyptians drowned in the Yam Suf and not the Nile.

en: The Mashgiach says the opportunity to thank Hashem, and the realization that it is a privilege, is itself one of Hashem's greatest gifts.
Thanks can never be finished: Tehillim ends with praise for every breath, and Nishmas says one cannot thank even for a single favor among thousands.
The four kinds of people who must thank are only samples, reminders that one must thank Hashem for everything.
Recognizing Hashem's hidden kindnesses takes a chacham who works on hakaras hatov, which is why Birkas HaGomel needs two Rabbanan.
Mitzvos of pirsumei nisa, publicizing a miracle, outweigh other mitzvos, and even women are obligated in them.
Gratitude is the greatest obligation in avodas Hashem: the more a person appreciates, the more of a tzaddik he becomes.
Hashem drowned the Egyptians in the Yam Suf and not in the Nile so that Jews could come to the place of the miracle and make a bracha.

title.en: Mizmor l'Sodah and Modim d'Rabbanan

summary.en: After a brief exchange before the shiur, the Mashgiach opens with Mizmor l'Sodah and calls the chance to thank Hashem one of His greatest gifts. He explains why each person says Modim d'Rabbanan himself, and that it ends with thanks for being able to thank.

title.en: For every breath: Tehillim and Nishmas

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Tehillim is mostly hoda'ah, and that David HaMelech ends it feeling he must thank for every breath. He brings Nishmas, that one cannot thank even for one favor, and describes the human body as a daily miracle.

title.en: The four who must thank are only samples

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the kapitel of Tehillim with the four who are rescued and must thank, and explains that they are only samples for thanking for everything. He brings the Gemara that Birkas HaGomel is said before ten with two Rabbanan, and says people notice their teeth only when they ache.

title.en: Why two Rabbanan at Birkas HaGomel

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that only a chacham who works on hakaras hatov sees Hashem's kindness in everything, even in what seems bad. Two are needed so that the second shows there is more to say after the first finished: thanking Hashem never ends.

title.en: The korban todah and pirsumei nisa

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the korban todah, unlike other shelamim, may be eaten only for a day and a night until chatzos, and brings the mefarshim that this makes the owner invite more people and publicize Hashem's kindness. He concludes that mitzvos of pirsumei nisa outweigh other mitzvos.

title.en: Chanukah, hidden miracles and gratitude

summary.en: With Chanukah approaching, the Mashgiach explains that owing thanks makes a person subordinate to his benefactor, that only Hashem knows the miracles He does daily, and that gratitude is the greatest obligation in avodas Hashem. He explains why women are obligated in Chanukah lights and the four cups, and begins the case of choosing between Kiddush wine and Chanukah lights.

title.en: The Chasam Sofer: why the Yam Suf and not the Nile

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer's question why the prohibition of returning to Mitzrayim is mentioned at the Yam Suf, and why the Egyptians were not drowned in the Nile, measure for measure. The answer: one makes a bracha at the place of a miracle, and since Jews may not return to Mitzrayim, Hashem made the miracle where they could come and thank Him.
